## Three-body and fall-off rate constants (`type: three-body` and fall-off types) {#sec-ch06-falloff}

### Summary

Some reactions need a collision partner that carries away energy without being changed: a third body, written `M`.
Its effect enters through an effective third-body concentration, the sum of all concentrations weighted by
species-specific collision efficiencies. At low pressure the rate grows linearly with that concentration; at high
pressure it saturates. The three-body form keeps only the low-pressure limit; the fall-off forms (Lindemann, Troe, SRI,
and the KB form read from KINETICS-base inputs) blend the two limits.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $[M]_{\mathrm{eff}}$, @eq-ch06-falloff-meff; three-body $k_0 [M]_{\mathrm{eff}}$; fall-off @eq-ch06-falloff-blend.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$]; efficiencies [-] (default 1); YAML $A$ in molecule, cm, s units.

**Placement.** Evaluators four to eight of `Kinetics.forward`, after Arrhenius, coagulation and evaporation.

**Activation.** `type: three-body`; `type: falloff` (Lindemann), with a `Troe` or an `SRI` block; KB only from KINETICS-base.

**Guarantee / limits.** Pointwise closed forms; Troe and SRI broadening differ from the published forms (Limits).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\varepsilon_{jn}$, collision efficiency of species $n$ in reaction $j$ [-]; $[M]_{\mathrm{eff}}$,
effective third-body concentration [mol m$^{-3}$]; $k_0$, low-pressure rate constant (units of a reaction one order
higher than written, without `M`); $k_\infty$, high-pressure rate constant; $P_r$, reduced pressure [-]; $F$, broadening
factor [-]; $F_{\mathrm{cent}}$, its centre value [-]. $c_n$ is the concentration of species $n$ (@sec-ch06-mass-action).

### Derivation

**Third body.** The effective third-body concentration of reaction $j$ is

$$
[M]_{\mathrm{eff},j} = \sum_n \varepsilon_{jn}\, c_n ,
$$ {#eq-ch06-falloff-meff}

with $\varepsilon_{jn}$ from the reaction's `efficiencies` map and 1 for every species not listed, gases and condensates
alike. A three-body reaction `A + B + M => AB + M` has rate constant $k = k_0(T)\, [M]_{\mathrm{eff}}$, with
$k_0 = A (T/T_{\mathrm{ref}})^{b} \exp(-E_a/T)$ as in @sec-ch06-arrhenius and $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ = 300 K; the mass-action
product of @sec-ch06-mass-action then supplies $c_A c_B$. `M` (or `(+M)`) is not a species: species registration
skips it, and it has no column of the stoichiometry matrix. @eq-ch06-falloff-meff is computed in `ThreeBodyImpl::forward`
({{< code src/kinetics/three_body.cpp ThreeBodyImpl::forward >}}) as the product of the concentrations with an
efficiency matrix built in `reset`.

**Fall-off.** With the reduced pressure $P_r = k_0 [M]_{\mathrm{eff}} / k_\infty$, the fall-off rate constant is the
Lindemann expression times a broadening factor:

$$
k = \frac{k_0 [M]_{\mathrm{eff}}}{1 + P_r}\, F .
$$ {#eq-ch06-falloff-blend}

For $P_r \to 0$ it tends to $k_0 [M]_{\mathrm{eff}} F$ and for $P_r \to \infty$ to $k_\infty F$.

**Where the Lindemann form comes from.** A unimolecular reaction $A \to P$ needs energy, which $A$ gains and loses
in collisions with any third body $M$. Lindemann's mechanism[^ch06-lindemann] writes this as two steps, with $A^*$ an
energized molecule:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A + M &\rightleftharpoons A^* + M \quad \text{rates } k_a, k_{-a} \\
A^* &\to P \quad \text{rate } k_b
\end{aligned}
$$

$A^*$ is short-lived, so its concentration is quasi-steady: it is made as fast as it is used,

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}[A^*]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k_a [A][M] - k_{-a} [A^*][M] - k_b [A^*] = 0 ,
$$

which gives $[A^*] = k_a [A][M] / (k_{-a}[M] + k_b)$. The product forms at the rate

$$
k_b [A^*] = \frac{k_a k_b [M]}{k_{-a}[M] + k_b}\, [A] = k\, [A] .
$$

At low pressure ($k_{-a}[M] \ll k_b$) every energized molecule reacts, and $k \to k_a [M]$. This identifies the
low-pressure constant $k_0 = k_a$, second order overall. At high pressure ($k_{-a}[M] \gg k_b$) activation is in
equilibrium, and $k \to k_a k_b / k_{-a} = k_\infty$. Dividing numerator and denominator by $k_b$ and substituting the
two limits,

$$
k = \frac{k_a [M]}{1 + k_{-a}[M]/k_b} = \frac{k_0 [M]}{1 + k_0 [M]/k_\infty} = \frac{k_0 [M]}{1 + P_r} ,
$$

which is @eq-ch06-falloff-blend with $F = 1$ and $[M] = [M]_{\mathrm{eff}}$. The broadening factors $F$ are empirical
corrections in $\log_{10} P_r$ to this two-state picture, and their parameters are fitted to data.[^ch06-troe]
Because $k_0$ multiplies one more concentration ($[M]$) than $k_\infty$, its input unit carries one more order. The
reader therefore converts $k_0$ with the order $n + 1$ in @eq-ch06-arrhenius-unit and $k_\infty$ with $n$
(`low-P-rate-constant` and `high-P-rate-constant` in `LindemannFalloffOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/kinetics/lindemann_falloff.cpp LindemannFalloffOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The check evaluates the
Lindemann rate constant for $P_r$ from $10^{-6}$ to $10^{6}$, with a third-body efficiency, against
$k_0 [M]/(1 + P_r)$, and reaches both limits to $10^{-6}$ at the ends of that range.[^ch06-check-c]
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch06-falloff-blend check_ch6_rates.py [c1] -->
Lindemann has $F = 1$
(`LindemannFalloffImpl::forward`, {{< code src/kinetics/lindemann_falloff.cpp LindemannFalloffImpl::forward >}}).
Troe and SRI both use

$$
\begin{aligned}
F &= F_{\mathrm{cent}}^{\,1/\left(1 + (\log_{10} P_r)^2\right)}, \\
F^{\mathrm{Troe}}_{\mathrm{cent}} &= (1 - a)\, e^{-T/T_3} + a\, e^{-T/T_1} + e^{-T_2/T}, \\
F^{\mathrm{SRI}}_{\mathrm{cent}} &= a\, e^{-b/T} + e^{-T/c} + d\, e^{-e/T},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-falloff-broadening}

where the last Troe term is present only when `T2` is non-zero and the last SRI term only when `E` is non-zero
(`compute_falloff_factor` in {{< code src/kinetics/troe_falloff.cpp TroeFalloffImpl::compute_falloff_factor >}} and
{{< code src/kinetics/sri_falloff.cpp SRIFalloffImpl::compute_falloff_factor >}}). $P_r$ is clamped to
$[10^{-300}, 10^{300}]$ and $F_{\mathrm{cent}}$ likewise. The KB form of KINETICS-base inputs is
$k = k_{\mathrm{low}}\, F / (1 + P_r)$ with $P_r = k_{\mathrm{low}}\, n / k_{\mathrm{high}}$, $n$ the total number
density (an explicit `number_density` field, else $\sum_n c_n$), $F = F_c^{1/(1 + (\log_{10} P_r)^2)}$ with one
constant $F_c$, and $k = 0$ where either limit is not positive (`KBFalloffImpl::forward`,
{{< code src/kinetics/kb_falloff.cpp KBFalloffImpl::forward >}}).

### Numerical method

All forms are pointwise in every cell. `Kinetics.forward` passes the concentrations expanded to one copy per reaction
with gradient tracking on, so $\partial k/\partial c$ (and $\partial k/\partial T$ with `evolve_temperature`) comes from
one backward pass through these formulas (@sec-ch06-jacobian); the third-body dependence of $k$ therefore enters the
Jacobian without a hand-written derivative.

The YAML keys: `rate-constant` (three-body) or `low-P-rate-constant` and `high-P-rate-constant` (fall-off), each with
`A`, `b`, and `Ea_R` or `Ea` with a unit (`cal`, `kJ`, `J`); `efficiencies` (species: value); `Troe` with `A`, `T3`,
`T1` and optional `T2`; `SRI` with `A`, `B`, `C` and optional `D`, `E`. $A$ is converted from molecule, cm, s units with
the reaction order counting `M` once (once more for $k_0$ of a fall-off reaction). A missing `Ea_R` and `Ea` gives
$E_a = 0$ here, unlike the 1 K default of @sec-ch06-arrhenius.

The fall-off figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

not in the species list.

: Tests of three-body and fall-off rate constants. {#tbl-ch06-falloff-tests}

The test names and assertions are read from `tests/test_falloff.cpp` at the pin. Only the three-body form is compared
with its closed form; the Lindemann, Troe and SRI tests assert only that the rate is non-zero, so
@eq-ch06-falloff-blend and @eq-ch06-falloff-broadening have no reference-value test (missing evidence). The test
`real_chemistry_sample_reaction_full` was not read for this section. The derivation checks measure
$4.4 \times 10^{-16}$ for `[c1]` and $1.0 \times 10^{-6}$ for both limits, the size of $P_r$ at the ends of the
range.[^ch06-check-c] The Troe and SRI broadening still has no reference-value test.

### Limits

The Troe broadening of @eq-ch06-falloff-broadening is
$\log F = \log F_{\mathrm{cent}} / (1 + (\log_{10} P_r)^2)$. The published Troe form (Gilbert, Luther and Troe 1983,
[doi:10.1002/bbpc.19830870218](https://doi.org/10.1002/bbpc.19830870218)) has

$$
\log F = \log F_{\mathrm{cent}} / \left(1 + \left[(\log_{10} P_r + c)/(N - d(\log_{10} P_r + c))\right]^2\right)
$$

with
$c = -0.4 - 0.67 \log_{10} F_{\mathrm{cent}}$, $N = 0.75 - 1.27 \log_{10} F_{\mathrm{cent}}$, $d = 0.14$; the code's
form is the case $c = 0$, $N = 1$, $d = 0$ (verified by reading). The SRI form of Stewart, Larson and Golden (1989,
[doi:10.1016/0010-2180(89)90084-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-2180(89)90084-9)) is
$F = \left[a e^{-b/T} + e^{-T/c}\right]^{X}$ with $X = 1/(1 + (\log_{10} P_r)^2)$, which the code reproduces with three
parameters; with `D` and `E` given, the code adds $d\, e^{-e/T}$ inside the bracket. Mechanism files whose five-parameter
SRI entries mean $d \left[\ldots\right]^X T^{e}$ would be evaluated differently; that such inputs are misread is a
hypothesis, not run. No test checks either broadening against reference values.

The efficiency matrix has one column per registry species in card order (@sec-ch02-species-registry), and `forward`
contracts it with the first columns of the concentration vector, which `Kinetics` orders gases first, then
condensates. When the kinetics species are not the first registry species in the same order, an efficiency is applied
to a different species (verified by reading `reset` and `forward`; the size of the effect is not measured, a
hypothesis). Unlisted species, condensates included, count with efficiency 1. The `Ea` string uses the rounded
constants 1.987 cal mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ and 8.314 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.
